metadata.name: SH Benchy - Measured Recreation
metadata.description: A complete 3DBenchy recreation built purely from measurements of the reference STL and the official brochure specs (60.0 x 31.0 x 48.0mm), across 51 iterations: 9-ring measured hull loft (spoon bow, upright bulwark, uniform 2.6mm rail, raked transom), stepped deck with 45-degree ramp, trapezium cabin with arches, aligned windows and unified 1.2mm double frames, helm with recessed wheel, trapezoid roof at the measured 5.5 degrees, chimney to exactly 48.00mm, hawsepipe eyes, rod holder and prop-shaft socket. The session then runs the full print pipeline: bake booleans, subdivide the hull, join, voxel-remesh at 0.15mm, smooth, re-drill the bores, engrave SH BENCHY into the flat bottom, verify watertightness, and export sh_benchy.stl.

commands.description: Set scene to millimeters.
Cleanup: wipe the whole scene for an idempotent replay. Batch delete is dependency-safe: boolean holders and their cutters are removed together (addon guard skips dependents within the same batch).

Hull loft with 9 rings: a 3mm-wide KEEL SPINE (so the bottom builds from true quads instead of one big cap n-gon that tented and crumpled under smoothing/subdivision), footprint/stem bottom, flare shoulder, upright wall top, rail widest point, rounded rail top (sharp 27.2 bow peak), rail inner edge (2.6mm rail width), deck outline, and the 3mm deck centerline spine. Both caps are now benign coplanar slivers. Flat aft deck at Z=8.5, 45-degree ramp X=7-14, foredeck gradient; stern is a straight raked transom from (-25, 0) to the rail.

Port hawsepipe: a true pipe now - the 6.4mm tube passes through the bulwark and lines the hole (flange face still protruding ~0.8mm outside), so the print-prep subdivision cannot pinch the hull's hole closed; the passage stays a clean 4mm bore.
Starboard hawsepipe, mirrored true pipe through the bulwark.
Port hawsepipe cutter: 4mm horizontal hole through flange and bulwark into the cockpit, matching the reference hole at (X=24, Z=20.5).
Starboard hawsepipe cutter, mirrored.
Drill port hawsepipe through the hull wall.
Drill starboard hawsepipe through the hull wall.
Open the port flange into a ring around the hole.
Open the starboard flange into a ring around the hole.

Fishing-rod holder: 3.6mm tube on the centerline, raked 21 degrees aft to follow the transom angle - base on the aft deck against the inner transom, top leaning out over the stern rail at Z=12.7 like the reference.
Cutter for the rod holder's small slanted blind hole (2mm dia, ~1.8 deep, does not reach the deck).
Drill the blind hole into the rod holder top.

Propeller-shaft hole cutter: 1.5mm blind hole (about 2mm deep) into the lower transom on the centerline at the measured reference spot (Z=2.6), axis along the transom normal - a slot for a separately printed propeller.
Drill the propeller-shaft slot into the stern.

Bridge shell as a side-view trapezium loft: bottom ring on the original footprint (X -7.8 to 8.2 at the deck), top ring extended outward (X -9.0, flush with the roof rear edge, to 11.5 at the front) with its edge sloping parallel to the roof underside so the reveal under the trapezoid roof stays even. Side walls remain vertical at plus-minus 8.65 so the arches and their frames are unaffected.
Interior cutter: hollows the bridge leaving 1.4mm walls and a 2mm ceiling, open at the bottom so the deck shows inside.
Side arch doorways, straight part: 8mm wide opening through both side walls, deck to Z=28 (arch sides measured at X -3.1 to 4.9 on the reference).
Side arch doorways, rounded top: 4mm radius half-round capping the arches at the measured apex Z=32.
Frame-only arch cutter, 0.15mm larger per side than the wall cutter so frame and shell cut faces never coincide (kills z-fighting on the jambs).
Frame-only arch crown cutter, 0.15mm larger radius than the wall cutter.

Front window: the brochure's 10.50 x 9.50mm rectangle with horizontal cut surfaces, top aligned with the arch apex and stern window at Z=32; reaches X=12 to pierce the forward-leaning trapezium wall at every height.

Front window double frame as a rotation-free loft (rotated cubes are swung about the world origin by older addon builds): a 1.2mm-thick plate whose faces follow the leaning front wall by construction - back face a uniform 0.45mm inside the wall, front 0.75mm proud, 12.9 x 11.8 overall for the 1.2mm border.
Frame-only window cutter, 0.15mm larger per side to avoid coincident faces with the wall opening.
Open the front window frame into a 1.2mm border ring.
Stern window flange: the brochure's 12mm outer ring on the bridge rear wall, standing 0.9mm proud like the other frames (0.3 embedded).
Stern window: 9mm hole through flange and rear wall (brochure inner diameter 9.00).

Roof: the brochure's 23.00mm slab at 5.5 degrees (front edge top Z=40.0, rear Z=37.8), but with the MEASURED trapezoid plan - flush with the walls at the rear (halfwidth 8.7) and flaring to 10.0 at the front visor - so the roof reads centered like the reference instead of rear-heavy.
Chimney body: 7mm diameter at the measured center X=-4, base embedded in the roof.
Chimney top collar, taking the model to the spec 48.00mm overall height.
Chimney blind hole: brochure spec 3.00mm diameter, 11.00mm deep from the top.
Deck box: brochure 12.00 x 10.81mm outside at the measured position (X -19.2 to -8.4), top at the spec 15.50mm.
Box pocket: brochure 8.00 x 7.00 inside, 9.00 deep from the top - cuts through the box floor into the deck (pocket floor at Z=6.5).
Hollow the bridge.
Cut the straight part of the side arches.
Round the arch tops.
Cut the front window.
Cut the stern window through the rear wall.
Open the stern flange into a ring.
Drill the chimney bore through the body.
Drill the chimney bore through the collar.
Continue the bore into the roof slab so the blind hole reaches the full spec 11.00mm depth (floor at Z=37).
Cut the box pocket.
Continue the pocket 2mm into the deck (spec depth 9.00 from box top).
Port arch frame, straight legs: 1.2mm-wide border plate standing 0.9mm proud of the side wall.
Port arch frame, rounded crown.
Starboard arch frame, straight legs.
Starboard arch frame, rounded crown.
Open the port frame legs, leaving the 1.2mm border.
Round the port frame opening.
Trim the port crown below the arch spring line.
Open the port crown into a ring.
Open the starboard frame legs.
Round the starboard frame opening.
Trim the starboard crown below the arch spring line.
Open the starboard crown into a ring.
Helm console plate on the inside of the front wall, fully below the front window sill (Z 13.5-20.5).
Steering wheel: 6.5mm disc facing aft, top edge just below the front window sill.
Recess cutter: sinks the wheel face 0.3mm inside the outer rim, leaving the raised ring like the real wheel.
Cut the sunken face into the wheel, between rim and hub.
Wheel hub knob inside the sunken face, its front flush with the outer rim plane.
Create red material.
Color hull, flanges, rod holder, superstructure, arch frames, and wheel red.
Bake hull booleans (hawsepipes, prop shaft slot, box pocket).

Subdivision surface on the hull only: turns the big low-poly facets into the continuously curved hull of the reference (also blends away the 0.6mm keel-strip seam at the bow). Cabin/roof/box stay crisp - they only need edge rounding.
Bake the hull subdivision.
Bake cabin booleans (interior, arches, windows).
Bake port eye flange ring.
Bake starboard eye flange ring.
Bake rod holder blind hole.
Bake stern window flange ring.
Bake chimney bore in the roof.
Bake chimney body bore.
Bake chimney collar bore.
Bake box pocket.
Bake port arch frame cuts.
Bake port arch crown cuts.
Bake starboard arch frame cuts.
Bake starboard arch crown cuts.
Bake front window frame ring.
Bake the wheel face recess.
Delete all spent cutters (every cutter name contains 'Cut'); safe now that all modifiers are baked.
Join all 18 visible parts into one object (reference 3DBenchy import stays separate).
Voxel remesh at 0.15mm - the size already proven to run on this machine (0.12 risked exhausting memory and crashing Blender mid-pipeline); the final smoothing pass handles the residual terracing.
Laplacian smoothing: erases the residual voxel terracing and rounds the remaining crisp edges (cabin, roof, box, frames); the hull is already curved and pre-smoothed.
Final port hawsepipe bore: subdivision pinches the hull's hole and the remesh unions the pinched material into the passage, so the 4mm bore is re-drilled through the finished solid.
Final starboard hawsepipe bore, mirrored.
Final propeller-shaft socket: re-drilled for the same reason (the 1.5mm blind hole is even more prone to closing under subdivision + remesh).
Re-drill the port eye through the smooth solid.
Re-drill the starboard eye.
Re-drill the propeller-shaft socket.

Bottom nameplate like the reference's CT3D.xyz: 4mm capitals lying face-down on the hull bottom, readable from below. Engraved rather than raised so the bottom stays perfectly flat on the print bed (the brochure's own shallow-letters trick).
Convert the FONT object to a mesh so it can act as a boolean cutter.
Engrave the name 0.25mm into the hull bottom - after remesh and smoothing, so the letters stay crisp.
Bake the final bores and the engraving into the mesh.
Waterproofing check: watertight / manifold / degenerate-geometry report before export.
Export the finished SH Benchy - smooth, watertight, engraved, print-ready.
